title: Validate the tactical AI against pure rules-as-written SF2E, not just the Frame/vehicle reskin
summary: Eventually pit real pregen PC characters against real, unmodified SF2E NPC statblocks (no 10x grid, no Frame/vehicle chassis, no Resonance/Bleed) using the same decide()/evaluateState AI, so that a fight's outcome can be checked against the SRD's own published XP-budget expectations instead of this project's own conjecture about what a fair fight looks like.
description:
Raised directly by Ingram while directing the design doc §18 archetype-battery fixes: "Ideally eventually you'd be able to do things like pitch a battle between a set of pure pregen PC characters and pure rules as written SF2E NPCs. The idea being that if you can do that and make use of all abilities and logic in the SF system using purely hand crafted examples of that system then you can start to relate success or failure to the XP budget which gives you real expectations of how things should go based not on our conjecture but rather the battle test maths of the Pathfinder/Starfinder RPG system."

Why this matters, stated precisely: every archetype in tools/battle-simulator/scenarios/archetypes.mjs (design doc §17-§18) uses SYNTHETIC statblocks built by hand against GM Core's by-level creature-building tables (AC/attack/damage/HP bands) — real numbers, but assembled by this project's own judgement about which band to pick for which role. The first archetype battery run found that battery's own party fixture was under-armored relative to those tables entirely by accident (three of four units below even the level-12 Low AC band), which the level-appropriate math itself only caught once actually checked line-by-line. A RAW validation layer would remove that whole class of error at the source: PCs built by the actual character-creation rules (feats, class features, real gear, real spell lists) fighting REAL published monsters, so if the AI wins/loses at roughly the rate the SRD's own encounter-difficulty table predicts, that is a genuine, external check that both the AI and this project's homebrew chassis/scale numbers are sound — not just internally consistent with each other.

This is NOT starting from nothing. Real groundwork already exists and is directly reusable:
- tools/character-builder/derive.mjs — the real SF2E level-1 chargen process, grounded in reference/srd/player-core/64-character-creation.json's actual steps, already tested against every Player Core class pregen's own published HP total.
- tools/character-builder/extract-pregen.mjs + tools/pack-extractor/read-pack.mjs — already extracts real pregen PCs directly from gamesystems/sf2e/packs/paizo-pregens (a real Foundry LevelDB compendium), used today to build the kid-fixtures and the Mystic Frame's real spell data (Eldritch Lance, Transfer Vitality, extracted verbatim from the 'Lunar-17' pregen).
- gamesystems/sf2e/packs/ also ships real bestiary compendiums (rulebook-bestiaries, alien-core-bestiary, starfinder-society-bestiary, and others) readable by the exact same pack-extractor tooling — real, unmodified NPC/monster statblocks, not hand-assembled band picks.
- reference/tables/encounter-and-rewards-math.json — the real XP-budget-by-relative-level table already used to cost every archetype in the current battery.

What this would actually need, honestly scoped (not started): a personnel-scale engine mode, since the current engine.mjs is built around the campaign's specific 10x-grid/50ft-square rescale (design/scale-and-chassis.md §14f) for Frame/vehicle combat specifically — RAW validation needs the real 5ft grid and real (not rescaled) ranges. It would also need real basic-action coverage beyond what's built (Step/Stride/Strike/spells/heals only today) and — a real, already-documented gap — SF2E's skill actions (Demoralize, Trip, Feint, Tumble Through) are NOT usably covered by the reference/srd/ mirror (player-core/167-skills.json is a 918-character stub), so a fully RAW-faithful PC would be missing real tactical options the SRD mirror simply doesn't have text for yet.
resolution: Phase 0-3 of the approved plan (design/scale-and-chassis.md §19) are built and tested: a real personnel-engine/ tree (5ft grid, ported not parametrized — resolves the first openSubQuestion below), a real synthetic 3-room test building, real extraction of both a level-1 Mystic pregen (Lunar-17) and a level-1 NPC (Security Goon, rulebook-bestiaries) with zero invented numbers, and a real fight between them that resolves legally across all three room configurations with a qualitatively-read, coherent transcript. NOT yet done: cross-checking this fight's outcome against reference/tables/encounter-and-rewards-math.json's own XP-budget predictions, a second matchup, save-based actions (skipped on both sides — real, cited, but inert), and skill actions in combat (the reference/srd/ gap this entry originally flagged is now closed — see Phase 0 in §19 — but nothing yet USES the mirrored skill-action text in a fight). Left in-progress, not done, because the idea's own broader ambition (XP-budget cross-referencing, multiple matchups) isn't exhausted yet.
sourceContext: User direction, 2026-08-23, immediately after asking for the three broken tactical archetypes (design doc §17) to be fixed and an ablation harness built (§18) — framed as "ideally eventually", a stated long-term direction rather than the turn's immediate ask.
openSubQuestions: Personnel-scale engine mode: a genuinely separate mode from the Frame/vehicle 10x-grid engine, or a parametrized FEET_PER_SQUARE the existing engine could run at 5ft for this purpose? Needs real investigation, not assumed either way.

Which bestiary pack(s) to draw from first, and whether extraction needs to handle monster-specific mechanics (Recall Knowledge DCs, elite/weak adjustments — CLAUDE.md already flags that no numeric elite/weak adjustment table was found anywhere in the mirrored text) that pregen extraction never had to.

Skill actions (Demoralize, Trip, Feint, Tumble Through) are a confirmed gap in the reference/srd/ mirror — build them from general SF2E knowledge (against this project's own standing rule preferring the mirror's exact numbers), find/mirror the missing source text first, or scope RAW validation to skip skill actions initially and note the gap explicitly?

Does this become a genuinely separate simulator (its own scenarios/ tree, its own fixtures) or a mode of the existing one? The scale-separation rule (design/scale-and-chassis.md §2) suggests separate, matching how ground-layer/ already stays out of engine/'s Frame-scale comparisons.
